---
title: "Differences from the original code"
format: html
---

This page lists every way the scripts on this site differ from the original analysis: a single R Markdown file of March 2021 (`Mayar_R_markdown_2021-3-1.Rmd`), which produced the figures and model results of the published article [@almohajer2021faceshield]. The original file is kept outside this repository.

Each entry is one of five kinds:

-   **Corrected**: a mistake in the original code, corrected here.
-   **Same result**: the code is written differently, and gives the same numbers and figures.
-   **Added**: something the original code did not do.
-   **Removed**: something the original code did that is no longer needed.
-   **Kept**: something in the original code that looks unusual, kept as it was so the code still matches what was published.

No entry changes the models, the weekly estimates or the published results; the one correction changes a legend label.

::: callout-note
## Status
The scripts have been checked by reading; they have not yet been run on the study data. "Same result" means the code is written to give the same numbers and figures as the original; that is to be confirmed on the first run.
:::

## Setup

| Original code | Kind | This analysis | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Loaded `reshape2`, `svglite`, `flextable`, `knitr` and `ggthemr` (not on CRAN), none of them used by the analysis, and loaded `dplyr` and `ggplot2` twice. | Removed | Only the packages the analysis uses are attached, once each ([Setup](setup.qmd#packages)). | None |
| Read the data from the working directory, with a reminder to set it (`#setwd here`). | Same result | The data folder is named by `COVID_IC_DATA_DIR` in `.Renviron` ([Setup](setup.qmd#where-the-data-are)). | None |
| Typed the 21 week labels out by hand in each of its ten plots; one label had a stray leading space (" May 11"). | Same result | Computed once from the first Monday ([Setup](setup.qmd#week-labels)). | None visible |
| Set the intervention at `Vertline <- 12.9999` and drew the red line at `Vertline - 0.5`, week 12.4999. | Same result | `intervention_week` is 13 and the line is at week 12.5 ([Setup](setup.qmd#plot-constants)). | None visible |

## Data

| Original code | Kind | This analysis | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Did not check the workbook's columns. | Added | Stops if any of the seven expected columns is missing, naming only the missing columns ([1. Data](prepare_data.qmd#the-weekly-surveillance-data)). | None |
| Attached the weekly intervals with `cbind()`, which relies on the rows staying in order. | Same result | Added by name with `mutate()` ([Functions](functions.qmd#weekly-estimates-with-exact-intervals)). | None |
| `Intervention` was `Week > 12.9999`. | Same result | `Week >= 13` ([1. Data](prepare_data.qmd#time-series-variables)). | None for whole-number weeks |
| Added two placeholder rows at week 12.9999, with no outcome data, so the plotted line could step at the intervention. The models dropped them because their outcomes were missing. | Removed | The fitted lines are built separately, with the step, by `build_fitted_line()` ([Functions](functions.qmd#the-fitted-line)). The data hold one row per week. | None |
| Placed each week in Figure 2 at one day before `Date2` (week 1) or two days before (other weeks), with no note of what `Date2` is. | Kept | The same rule, with a note: `Date2` is the last day of each week's range, as recalled by the author ([1. Data](prepare_data.qmd#plot-dates)). | None |
| Read the Harris County file with `read.table()` and the date format `"%m / %d / %y"`. | Same result | `read_csv()`, with the date read as text and converted with `"%m/%d/%y"`; R reads a space in a date format as "zero or more spaces", so both formats read `07/05/20` the same way ([1. Data](prepare_data.qmd#harris-county-cases)). | None |
| A sentence meant to report the total number of tests and positives printed the R code instead of the numbers (its inline code lacked the `r`). | Removed | Not reproduced; the article reports the totals. | None |

## Models

| Original code | Kind | This analysis | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wrote out each of the eight models (`logistic1` to `logistic4`, `poisson1` to `poisson4`) in its own code chunk. | Same result | Each model's terms are written once and fitted for both outcomes; the models are kept in named lists ([2. Models](models.qmd#the-four-models)). | None |
| Fitted the exploratory models on `Week` and the published model on `Week2` (week minus 13). | Kept | As in the original. The exploratory models have no interaction, so centring the week would change only their intercepts, not their fit or their other coefficients. | None |
| Printed `summary()` for every model, and converted every table but one (the second HAI model) to a flextable. | Removed | The tables are `gtsummary` tables throughout ([2. Models](models.qmd#model-tables)). | None |
| Did not compute the values at week 13 that the article reports; they were read from the model output. | Added | `predict_at_intervention_week()` computes them from the published model ([2. Models](models.qmd#values-at-week-13)). | None, if they match the article; to be confirmed on the first run |
| The weeks spanned by the fitted lines followed the data rows. | Same result | Taken from the first and last week in the data ([2. Models](models.qmd#fitted-lines)). | None |

## Figures

| Original code | Kind | This analysis | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ten near-identical `ggplot()` calls. | Same result | One function, `plot_weekly_series()` ([Functions](functions.qmd#plotting-a-weekly-series)). | None for Figure 1 |
| The exploratory plots had a different point-size range, legend position and axis-title size from Figure 1. | Same result | The exploratory plots share Figure 1's styling ([3. Figures](figures.qmd#the-exploratory-models)). | The exploratory plots look slightly different; they were not published |
| Figure 1A's size legend read "# patients tested", although the points are sized by healthcare-personnel tests. Figure 2A had the same label. | Corrected | "# HCP tests" in both ([3. Figures](figures.qmd#figure-1)). | The legend text of Figures 1A and 2A |
| Figure 2's fitted line joined the predictions at the observed weeks, so it showed no step at the intervention, unlike Figure 1. | Kept | As in the original ([3. Figures](figures.qmd#figure-2-lines-by-date)). | None |
| Figure 2's red line was placed with `as.Date("07/05/2020", format = "%m / %d / %y", size = 1)`; the `size = 1` was passed to `as.Date()`, which ignores it. | Same result | `intervention_start - 1`, the same date ([3. Figures](figures.qmd#figure-2-lines-by-date)). | None |
| Drew the Harris County bars with `geom_bar(stat = "identity")`. | Same result | `geom_col()`, which is the same thing ([3. Figures](figures.qmd#figure-2)). | None |
| Saved Figure 1's panels as "Fig 1A 2020-9-19.tiff" and "Fig 1B 2020-9-19.tiff" in the working directory, with no size set. Figure 2 was not saved. | Added | All three figures are saved to `figures/` as `figure_1a.tiff`, `figure_1b.tiff` and `figure_2.tiff`, still with no size set, so their size depends on the graphics device ([3. Figures](figures.qmd#saving-the-figures)). | None |
